name: Uusikaupunki
title: Uusikaupunki Hull Gauging | UTM for Ro-Ro and Car Carriers
description: Thickness gauging in Uusikaupunki for ro-ro ships, car carriers and fertiliser trade bulkers at Hepokari and Yara: deck, ramp, hold and tank UTM.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ro-Ro, Vehicle and Bulk Ships in Uusikaupunki
intro: Uusikaupunki is a small town with a busy cargo harbour where the Bothnian Sea meets the Archipelago Sea. Hepokari harbour is built around ro-ro traffic and has long been Finland's main export port for cars from the Valmet Automotive plant, while the Yara fertiliser plant runs its own harbour for bulk and liquid cargoes. Ships here work cargo over a planned call, and that is when hull and deck readings fit in. Our technicians are flown out from India for each job.

highlights.h: Ro-ro and vehicle decks at Hepokari
highlights.p: Ro-ro ships and car carriers at Hepokari load over stern ramps onto several decks. Deck plating, ramp structure and hoistable-deck supports wear under constant wheeled traffic, and readings can be taken in the hours when a deck lies empty between discharge and loading.

highlights.h: Fertiliser cargoes at the Yara harbour
highlights.p: Ships serving the fertiliser plant carry raw materials and finished products that turn aggressive towards steel once damp. Hold coatings, frames and tank tops on these ships deserve closer readings than their age alone would suggest, and so does any pipework handling liquid cargo.

highlights.h: A short passage to the docking yard
highlights.p: Uusikaupunki has no merchant dry dock, but the yards at Rauma and Naantali are close by. A steel estimate measured during a cargo call here lets the owner arrive at either yard with renewal quantities already established.

port.h: Uusikaupunki's ro-ro harbour and industrial berths
p: Uusikaupunki sits on the south-west coast between Rauma and Turku, where the open Bothnian Sea gives way to the first islands of the Archipelago Sea. Its cargo harbour at Hepokari lies outside the old town and is reached by a fairway that was deepened in 2015 so that larger ships could call. The port's identity is ro-ro: it is equipped for stern-loading ships, has shipped export cars from the town's automotive plant for many years, and also handles conventional, project and liquid cargo. Forest products and industrial goods leave over the same quays. Nearby, the Yara fertiliser plant operates its own harbour for the raw materials it brings in and the products it sends out, so the town sees both wheeled and bulk traffic.

The ship types follow from that. Ro-ro cargo ships and car carriers on Baltic and North Sea routes make up a large share of calls, alongside multipurpose and general cargo ships for project and forest cargoes, and dry bulk carriers and chemical tankers for the fertiliser plant. Calls are planned rather than casual: a ro-ro ship arrives to an agreed loading list, a bulk carrier discharges to the plant's schedule, and a car carrier's stay depends on how many units are waiting on the quay. Smaller ships and coasters predominate, which suits the port's scale and its fairway. For a gauging crew this means modest-sized ships with clearly bounded windows, where the scope can be fixed before arrival and finished within the call.

Winter is part of life here, as everywhere on the Finnish coast. Ice usually builds up in the inner fairway and among the islands, and Finnish winter traffic restrictions decide which ice classes receive icebreaker assistance, so the regular ro-ro tonnage on Uusikaupunki routes is normally ice-classed. Ice abrades the bow and the waterline, and ro-ro ships, which berth stern-first many times a year, also show wear at the stern, the ramp landing and along the fender line. Summer brings the easiest access, with long daylight for deck and external work, and is when owners prefer to send a team for anything outside the hull. Ships waiting for a berth anchor off the harbour, with transfers by launch when conditions permit.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in and around Uusikaupunki
p: At Hepokari the work is done alongside, around the cargo plan. On ro-ro ships and car carriers, decks are measured as they empty, starting with the lowest deck if the discharge sequence allows, and stern ramps and their hinges are gauged and crack-tested while the ramp is down and clear of traffic. Multipurpose ships at the conventional berths give access to holds and hatch covers between cargo operations. Tank work on any ship depends on the crew ventilating and certifying spaces before the team arrives, so the list of tanks to be opened is agreed a day or two ahead with the chief officer.

The Yara harbour is an industrial berth under the plant's safety regime, and access for an inspection team is arranged by the agent with the plant as well as with the ship. Bulk carriers there can have holds, frames and tank tops measured once they are empty, and chemical tankers can have deck, piping and safe voids gauged within their permit system. For dockings, owners use the shipyard at Rauma or Turku Repair Yard at Naantali, both within easy reach, or yards further across the Baltic; gauging done at Uusikaupunki beforehand goes with the ship and saves days once it is in the dock.

Hepokari conventional quays — holds, tween decks and hatch covers on multipurpose ships carrying forest and project cargo

context.h: Port state control and cargo-driven corrosion at Uusikaupunki
p: Ships calling at Uusikaupunki come under Paris MoU port state control, which Traficom, the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency, carries out for Finland. On ro-ro ships, inspectors look at doors, ramps and watertight integrity as well as structure, so wastage and cracks around the stern ramp and its hinges are worth finding before an inspector does. The EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime both apply to the intra-EU voyages that make up most of this port's traffic, and under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation ships of 500 gross tonnage and upwards calling here, whatever their flag, must carry an up-to-date Inventory of Hazardous Materials, often revised when steel is renewed or equipment replaced.

Fertiliser trades bring their own corrosion pattern. Many fertiliser materials attract moisture, and residues left in holds form corrosive solutions on tank tops, in hopper corners and along frame brackets, while liquid feedstocks for fertiliser production move in tankers with their own survey regimes. Bulk carriers in these trades fall under the Enhanced Survey Programme like any other bulk carrier, but the cargo means wastage can gather in the lower holds earlier than the survey cycle assumes. For ice-classed ro-ro ships, the Finnish-Swedish Ice Class Rules tie the ship's winter access to its ice-belt scantlings, and readings there support the decision to keep a ship on a year-round service.

jobs.h: Gauging jobs we expect at Uusikaupunki
jobs.p: Work here is mostly sized to a single call. Ro-ro owners ask for vehicle-deck and ramp readings, often with crack detection, to support an annual or intermediate survey or to plan steel ahead of a docking. Bulk carriers serving the fertiliser plant bring hold and ballast tank scopes, where the cargo makes measured figures more useful than assumptions. Multipurpose ships bring hatch-cover and hold work during project or forest cargo operations. With docking yards so close, pre-docking estimates make particular sense here: completed afloat during the call, sent to the yard the same week, and checked a few days later once the ship is in the dock.

Lower hold, hopper and tank-top gauging on a bulk carrier after it discharges fertiliser raw materials at the Yara harbour
Hatch covers, coamings and tween decks on a multipurpose ship loading project cargo
Pre-docking steel estimate on an ice-class ro-ro before it moves to Rauma or Naantali for dry-docking

logistics: The team normally lands at Helsinki-Vantaa and drives west, or uses Turku Airport where connections suit, since Uusikaupunki is a short road journey north-west of Turku. The ship's agent arranges ISPS access at Hepokari, and at the Yara harbour also clears the team with the plant's own safety organisation; a launch is booked through the agent for anchorage work. Finland requires a Schengen visa for our India-based technicians, so dates are confirmed as soon as the call or loading slot is fixed, with time allowed for the consulate.
vessels: Dry bulk carriers in the fertiliser trade

faqs.q: Can a car carrier be gauged at Hepokari during a single loading call?
faqs.a: A defined scope can be. Decks that are empty before loading are measured first, together with the stern ramp while it is clear of traffic, and a few ballast tanks prepared by the crew can be added. We agree the order with the chief officer so that each deck is finished before cars are driven on, and anything not reached is listed for the next call.

faqs.q: Why do fertiliser cargoes call for closer gauging?
faqs.a: Because their residues become corrosive once they take up moisture. On bulk carriers in this trade the tank top, the hopper corners and the lower frame brackets can thin faster than the ship's age suggests, especially where coatings have broken down. Measuring those areas on a close pattern gives the owner and the surveyor real figures for planning steel renewal and coating repairs.

faqs.q: Where do ships calling at Uusikaupunki go for dry-docking?
faqs.a: The nearest merchant docking yards are at Rauma, up the coast, and at Naantali near Turku, and many owners also dock in Poland or the Baltic states. A steel estimate measured during the Uusikaupunki call can be sent to the yard before the ship arrives, and our team can continue to the yard to finish the programme in the dock if the owner prefers.

faqs.q: Can stern ramps and hinges be crack-tested as well as gauged?
faqs.a: Yes. Magnetic particle testing at stern-ramp hinges, ramp-to-deck connections and hoistable-deck supports is a common addition to deck gauging on ro-ro ships and vehicle carriers, because fatigue cracks at those points can appear well before plate wastage does. The crew needs to clean the areas and keep the ramp clear of traffic while the test is carried out.
